children: Waaree Renewable Technologies has entered the data-centre infrastructure segment through a new subsidiary, seeking to tap rising demand for power-intensive digital infrastructure and AI computing

Waaree Renewable Technologies Ltd has expanded beyond its core renewable-energy business into data-centre infrastructure with the incorporation of Sunstar Data Centers Private Limited, a wholly owned step-down subsidiary. The new entity was incorporated on 11 September 2026 and will focus on data-centre infrastructure, including hyperscale, AI-ready, edge and cloud facilities.

The move comes as India's data-centre industry enters a high-growth phase, driven by artificial intelligence, cloud adoption, digital services and rising data consumption. The expansion also creates a strategic link between renewable power development and the rapidly increasing electricity requirements of data centres.

India's installed data-centre capacity stood at around 1.5 GW in 2025 and is projected to reach 4.5–6.5 GW by 2030, according to the Council on Energy, Environment and Water.  The Ministry of Power estimates that electricity demand from data centres could reach 13.56 GW by 2031–32.

This is making reliable, scalable and increasingly renewable power a critical consideration for data-centre developers. The wider economic trend is also reflected in the growing data-centre power market. Industry estimates put India's data-centre power market at USD 1.16 billion in 2026, with the market projected to reach USD 2.64 billion by 2031.

For renewable-energy companies, the shift towards data centres presents an opportunity to move further up the value chain by combining power generation, infrastructure and digital-energy requirements. Industry experts say the convergence of renewable energy and data centres is likely to become increasingly important as AI workloads raise electricity requirements, while large customers seek more reliable and lower-carbon power sources.

Globally, data-centre electricity consumption is projected to grow by around 15 per cent annually between 2024 and 2030, more than four times the growth rate of electricity consumption from other sectors, according to the International Energy Agency. Waaree's entry therefore comes at a time when India's digital infrastructure expansion is increasingly becoming an energy-infrastructure opportunity, potentially creating new avenues for renewable developers beyond conventional solar and power projects.
